title: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-03-21

Opens [Gal 2](/bible/galatians/2) · [Gal 3](/bible/galatians/3) · [Heb 9](/bible/hebrews/9) · [Heb 10](/bible/hebrews/10) · [Sir 15](/bible/sirach/15) · [Isa 19](/bible/isaiah/19) · [Gal 5](/bible/galatians/5) · [Acts 15](/bible/acts/15) · [Lev 12](/bible/leviticus/12) · [Rom 2](/bible/romans/2) · [Rom 8](/bible/romans/8) · [2 Cor 3](/bible/2-corinthians/3) · [James 2](/bible/james/2)
## Introduction *[[6:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=414s)]* The next lesson in the series navigating through Paul's letters, on the works of the law and liberty. The last class was left open-ended on purpose so the Christian commenters would bring their verses, and this one dismantles them: the works of the law in Galatians is the law of sacrifice, the curse is the condemnation of Deuteronomy 27 that no animal could atone, Hebrews 9 and 10 show Christ offered once for all and a testament in force only after the testator dies, circumcision after the manner of Moses is circumcision with sacrifice, and the law of sin and death and the ministration of death are the same sacrifice Christ freed us from. Then Romans 2, James 1 and 2, Romans 13 and Mark 12: the doers of the law are justified, the royal law is love thy neighbour, obedience is better than sacrifice, and faith without works is dead. ## In The News - *[[2:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=150s)]* **The AI thumbnail animation: Paul against the men saying except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses ye cannot be saved** — The argument of the whole class in a minute: a yoke we were not able to bear, and grace reigning through righteousness unto eternal life by Christ. ## Scriptures Opened **[Galatians 2:16](/bible/galatians/2#v16)** *[[8:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=499s)]* > [16](/bible/galatians/2#v16) Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. - By the works of the law shall no flesh be justified: the verse the Christians run to, and the class will show which law Paul means. **[Galatians 3:1-13](/bible/galatians/3#v1)** *[[8:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=530s)]* > [1](/bible/galatians/3#v1) O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? > > [2](/bible/galatians/3#v2) This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? > > [3](/bible/galatians/3#v3) Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? > > [4](/bible/galatians/3#v4) Have ye suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain. > > [5](/bible/galatians/3#v5) He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? > > [6](/bible/galatians/3#v6) Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. > > [7](/bible/galatians/3#v7) Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. > > [8](/bible/galatians/3#v8) And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed. > > [9](/bible/galatians/3#v9) So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. > > [10](/bible/galatians/3#v10) For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. > > [11](/bible/galatians/3#v11) But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith. > > [12](/bible/galatians/3#v12) And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them. > > [13](/bible/galatians/3#v13) Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree: - Who hath bewitched you: the Pharisees of Acts 15, false brethren brought in unawares, were spreading the doctrine that animal sacrifice mattered more than Christ's. Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law or by the hearing of faith; having begun in the Spirit are ye made perfect by the flesh, the flesh of the animals. - Abraham believed God and it was accounted for righteousness: his faith came before his sacrificing, believing the land and the son in his old age. They which are of faith are the children of Abraham, and the heathen God justifies through faith are the scattered northern kingdom, covered last lesson. - As many as are of the works of the law are under the curse, for cursed is everyone that continueth not in all things written in the book of the law: the curse is condemnation, the death for idolatry, adultery, murder and the rest that no animal could atone. The Galatians came in hearing Christ had died and redeemed them from sins the animals could not cover, and the scattered Israelites were rooted in idolatry, so under the old covenant they were simply condemned. - The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom. Precepts: - **[Deuteronomy 27:15-26](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v15)** > [15](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v15) Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen. > > [16](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v16) Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [17](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v17) Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [18](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v18) Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of the way. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [19](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v19) Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [20](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v20) Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife; because he uncovereth his father’s skirt. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [21](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v21) Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [22](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v22) Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [23](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v23) Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [24](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v24) Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [25](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v25) Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen. > > [26](/bible/deuteronomy/27#v26) Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that maketh a graven image, dishonours his parents, removes the landmark, lies with a beast or his sister, takes reward to slay the innocent, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law; all the people said amen. Moral law, loving thy neighbour, agreed to on pain of death, and that is where Galatians 3:10 quotes from. - **[Habakkuk 2:4](/bible/habakkuk/2#v4)** > [4](/bible/habakkuk/2#v4) Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith. His soul which is lifted up is not upright in him, that is Esau; but the just shall live by his faith, which Paul quotes, and the just are those keeping the law, holy, just and good. - **[Romans 7:12](/bible/romans/7#v12)** > [12](/bible/romans/7#v12) Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. The law is holy and the commandment holy, just and good: what makes you just, and the just live by faith in Christ. - **[John 11:49-50](/bible/john/11#v49)** > [49](/bible/john/11#v49) And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, > > [50](/bible/john/11#v50) Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. Caiaphas: it is expedient that one man die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Both kingdoms were condemned under the covenant they kept violating, and that is the curse of the law Christ died to take us out of. **[Hebrews 9:9-22](/bible/hebrews/9#v9)** *[[17:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=1049s)]* > [9](/bible/hebrews/9#v9) Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; > > [10](/bible/hebrews/9#v10) Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. > > [11](/bible/hebrews/9#v11) But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; > > [12](/bible/hebrews/9#v12) Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. > > [13](/bible/hebrews/9#v13) For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: > > [14](/bible/hebrews/9#v14) How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? > > [15](/bible/hebrews/9#v15) And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. > > [16](/bible/hebrews/9#v16) For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. > > [17](/bible/hebrews/9#v17) For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. > > [18](/bible/hebrews/9#v18) Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. > > [19](/bible/hebrews/9#v19) For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, > > [20](/bible/hebrews/9#v20) Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. > > [21](/bible/hebrews/9#v21) Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. > > [22](/bible/hebrews/9#v22) And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. - Gifts and sacrifices that could not make him that did the service perfect, meats and drinks, divers washings and carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation: the sacrifices were imposed on us until Christ died and became high priest. - By a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, by his own blood, he entered in once into the holy place in the heavens and obtained eternal redemption, where the animals had to be offered constantly. Paul was preparing them: when the temple is destroyed and the priests are gone, what will you do if you are still bound to that? - If the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean purified the flesh, that is baptism, what John the Levite did in the Jordan outside the temple; how much more shall the blood of Christ purge your conscience from dead works. Christ's blood supersedes water. - He is the mediator of the new testament for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament: the us of eternal redemption is Israel, and that destroys John 3:16 as all nations. - Where a testament is there must be the death of the testator: the Old Testament is Christ's will, prophesying his death, the ships, the scattering, America out of Rome, all set in motion when he died. A testament is of force after men are dead, so if we are still under the old covenant Christ has to die a second time. - Moses sprinkled the book and all the people with blood and water, scarlet wool and hyssop, the purification with blood, and almost all things are purged with blood: almost, because no animal could be offered for idolatry, bestiality, murder, adultery or Sabbath breaking, and without shedding of blood is no remission. Remission is your sin put on pause, like cancer, because the scapegoat died in your stead. **[Hebrews 10:1-18](/bible/hebrews/10#v1)** *[[34:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=2059s)]* > [1](/bible/hebrews/10#v1) For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. > > [2](/bible/hebrews/10#v2) For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins. > > [3](/bible/hebrews/10#v3) But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year. > > [4](/bible/hebrews/10#v4) For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. > > [5](/bible/hebrews/10#v5) Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: > > [6](/bible/hebrews/10#v6) In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. > > [7](/bible/hebrews/10#v7) Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. > > [8](/bible/hebrews/10#v8) Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; > > [9](/bible/hebrews/10#v9) Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. > > [10](/bible/hebrews/10#v10) By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. > > [11](/bible/hebrews/10#v11) And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: > > [12](/bible/hebrews/10#v12) But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; > > [13](/bible/hebrews/10#v13) From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. > > [14](/bible/hebrews/10#v14) For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified. > > [15](/bible/hebrews/10#v15) Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before, > > [16](/bible/hebrews/10#v16) This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; > > [17](/bible/hebrews/10#v17) And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. > > [18](/bible/hebrews/10#v18) Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. - The context has not changed from chapter 9: the law with a shadow of good things to come is the law of sacrifice, offered year by year, which can never make the comers thereunto perfect, or they would have ceased to be offered. The animal dying for you was meant to make you stop sinning, but we are sinful by nature. - Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: Christ speaking through David in Psalm 40 of what he would do on the earth, which are offered by the law, the same works of the law Paul means in Galatians. He taketh away the first that he may establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. - This man, after one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God expecting till his enemies be made his footstool: the king of kings has a throne and is not standing on punishment. - The covenant after those days, my laws in their hearts, is the kingdom with the new bodies that keep them perfectly; and where remission of these is there is no more offering for sin, so once Christ died there was no need of animals though the temple still stood. **[Sirach 15:15](/bible/sirach/15#v15)** *[[47:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=2849s)]* > [15](/bible/sirach/15#v15) If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness. - If thou wilt, to keep the commandments and to perform acceptable faithfulness: keeping the commandments is performing faithfulness, so your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works. That was what the last class left out for the commenters. Precepts: - **[Sirach 19:20](/bible/sirach/19#v20)** > [20](/bible/sirach/19#v20) The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency. The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: acceptable faithfulness. - **[Genesis 26:5](/bible/genesis/26#v5)** > [5](/bible/genesis/26#v5) Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. Because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my laws: past tense, what he was doing that proved his faith. **[Galatians 3:23-29](/bible/galatians/3#v23)** *[[55:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=3300s)]* > [23](/bible/galatians/3#v23) But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. > > [24](/bible/galatians/3#v24) Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. > > [25](/bible/galatians/3#v25) But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. > > [26](/bible/galatians/3#v26) For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. > > [27](/bible/galatians/3#v27) For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. > > [28](/bible/galatians/3#v28) There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. > > [29](/bible/galatians/3#v29) And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise. - Before faith came we, Israel, were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith afterward revealed, as Hebrews 9 says imposed until the reformation. The law of sacrifice was our schoolmaster, the placeholder, to bring us to Christ that we might be justified by faith in his death, and after faith is come we are no longer under it. - Ye who were kept under the law are all the children of God by faith in Christ, whether Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female, the same people in different conditions. If ye be Christ's then are ye Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise, and the promise pertains to Israel; name me one other nation God calls his people in the Old Testament. Precepts: - **[Romans 8:3](/bible/romans/8#v3)** > [3](/bible/romans/8#v3) For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: What the law could not do in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending his Son and condemned sin in the flesh: he ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by his death. - **[Hebrews 7:18-19](/bible/hebrews/7#v18)** > [18](/bible/hebrews/7#v18) For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof. > > [19](/bible/hebrews/7#v19) For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God. A disannulling of the commandment for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof, for the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope, Christ, did: the annulled commandment is sacrifice. **[Isaiah 19:25](/bible/isaiah/19#v25)** *[[1:02:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=3773s)]* > [25](/bible/isaiah/19#v25) Whom the Lord of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance. - Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria. Precepts: - **[Isaiah 27:12-13](/bible/isaiah/27#v12)** > [12](/bible/isaiah/27#v12) And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel. > > [13](/bible/isaiah/27#v13) And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem. The Lord gathers one by one all ye children of Israel, and they come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt: that is who Egypt my people is. - **[Isaiah 11:11](/bible/isaiah/11#v11)** > [11](/bible/isaiah/11#v11) And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. The remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea. - **[Zechariah 10:6-10](/bible/zechariah/10#v6)** > [6](/bible/zechariah/10#v6) And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the Lord their God, and will hear them. > > [7](/bible/zechariah/10#v7) And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad; their heart shall rejoice in the Lord. > > [8](/bible/zechariah/10#v8) I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them: and they shall increase as they have increased. > > [9](/bible/zechariah/10#v9) And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again. > > [10](/bible/zechariah/10#v10) I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them. I will save the house of Joseph and bring them again, and they shall be as though I had not cast them off; I will hiss for them and gather them, and bring them again out of the land of Egypt and out of Assyria. **[Galatians 5:1-4](/bible/galatians/5#v1)** *[[1:08:27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=4107s)]* > [1](/bible/galatians/5#v1) Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage. > > [2](/bible/galatians/5#v2) Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing. > > [3](/bible/galatians/5#v3) For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law. > > [4](/bible/galatians/5#v4) Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace. - Stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage: the yoke is sacrifice, and had we stayed under it we would all be destroyed once the temple fell and the priests were scattered with no way to atone. - If ye be circumcised, after the manner of Moses, Christ shall profit you nothing, and every man so circumcised is a debtor to do the whole law, including the sacrifices, with the temple about to be destroyed. Whosoever is justified by the law, sacrifice coupled with circumcision, is fallen from grace: relying on animals is rejecting Christ's sacrifice, bewitched by the Pharisees of Acts 15 or men like them. The Christian reads this as no commandments and no Sabbath. **[Acts 15:1-10](/bible/acts/15#v1)** *[[1:10:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=4208s)]* > [1](/bible/acts/15#v1) And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved. > > [2](/bible/acts/15#v2) When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question. > > [3](/bible/acts/15#v3) And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren. > > [4](/bible/acts/15#v4) And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them. > > [5](/bible/acts/15#v5) But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses. > > [6](/bible/acts/15#v6) And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter. > > [7](/bible/acts/15#v7) And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. > > [8](/bible/acts/15#v8) And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; > > [9](/bible/acts/15#v9) And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. > > [10](/bible/acts/15#v10) Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? - Certain men from Judaea taught except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses ye cannot be saved, and verse five names them: the sect of the Pharisees which believed, whose livelihood was sacrificing, like the pastors today afraid that this Christ takes their money. - Peter: God put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith; why tempt ye God to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear. Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. ## Class Questions - **Which law is Galatians about, and which law is Romans 2:13 about?** Galatians is the law of sacrifice, elaborated in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, and Romans 2 is the commandments; faith comes first and the works follow. - **What is the law of sin and death?** The old law of sacrifice: if you sinned a certain sin under Moses you were condemned to death, with no animal to atone and no I'm sorry. - **What is the yoke of bondage?** Sacrifice, imposed on us until the time of reformation, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear. - **Name a nation besides Israel that God calls his people in the Old Testament.** There is none; Egypt my people and Assyria my people in Isaiah 19 are Israel in those lands, as Isaiah 27, Isaiah 11 and Zechariah 10 show. ## In Closing *[[2:21:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xuIqTWwXmA&t=8464s)]* As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
